problem: What is the quotient of $2{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-1$ divided by $2{x}^{2}+1?$
worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
2{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-1=2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-1 \\  & 2{x}^{2}+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-\,2{x}^{2}+0x-1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,\,2{x}^{2}+0x-1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}-1,$ and

- the remainder is $0.$
